city: San Lorenzo de El Escorial, Madrid

manuscripts.title_arabic: كتاب التصريف لمن عجز عن التأليف (المقالة الثلاثون)
manuscripts.title_translit: Kitāb al-Taṣrīf li-man ʿajiza ʿan al-taʾlīf (Maqāla 30)
manuscripts.title_turkish: Kitâbü't-Tasrîf - 30. Makale: el-Amel bi'l-Yed (Cerrahi ve Aletler)
manuscripts.author: Ebû'l-Kâsım Halef bin Abbâs ez-Zehrâvî (Abulcasis)
manuscripts.illustration_description: Over 200 ink drawings of surgical instruments, cauteries, scalpels, bone saws, vaginal speculums, and catheters.
manuscripts.subject: Medicine & Surgery
manuscripts.latin_translation: Chirurgia (translated by Gerard of Cremona in Toledo, 12th c.)
manuscripts.historical_importance: The founding surgical manual of European medicine; introduced catgut internal suturing, lithotomy positions, and detailed mechanical instrument morphology.
references: Derenbourg, H., Les manuscrits arabes de l'Escurial, Paris, 1884
Spink & Lewis, Albucasis on Surgery and Instruments, 1973

manuscripts.title_turkish: Tuleytula Zîci ve Evrensel Usturlap Risalesi
manuscripts.author: Ebû İshâk İbrâhîm bin Yahyâ ez-Zerkâlî (Arzachel)
manuscripts.illustration_description: Geometric projection drawings of the azafea (universal astrolabe) stereographic projection without latitude plate dependency.
manuscripts.subject: Astronomy & Mathematics
manuscripts.latin_translation: Tabulae Toletanae & Canones Arzachelis (Gerard of Cremona / John of Brescia)
manuscripts.historical_importance: Corrected Mediterranean longitudinal dimension from Ptolemy's 62° to 42°; proved the motion of solar apogee (12.04 arcseconds/year).
references: Toomer, G. J., The Solar Theory of az-Zarqal, Centaurus, 1969
Puig, R., Los Tratados de la Azafea, Madrid, 1987

manuscripts.author: Ebû Zekeriyyâ Yahyâ bin Muhammed b. el-Avvâm el-İşbîlî
manuscripts.illustration_description: None, contains detailed tables of soil strata, seasonal irrigation regimes, and grafting charts.
manuscripts.subject: Agronomy & Hydraulic Engineering
manuscripts.latin_translation: Libro de Agricultura (translated into Spanish by Banqueri, 1802)
manuscripts.historical_importance: The most comprehensive medieval treatise on agronomy; describes 585 cultivated plants, 50+ fruit trees, soil pedology, and drip irrigation using porous terracotta vessels.
references: Banqueri, J. A., Libro de Agricultura, Madrid, 1802
García Sánchez, E., El tratado agrícola de Ibn al-Awwam, 1992

manuscripts.author: Ebû'l-Velîd Muhammed bin Ahmed bin Rüşd (Averroes)
manuscripts.illustration_description: Marginal scholia and philosophical glosses in Maghrebi script.
manuscripts.subject: Rationalist Philosophy & Epistemology
manuscripts.historical_importance: Systematic rebuttal of Al-Ghazali's Tahafut al-Falasifa; rigorous defence of causality, necessary connection, and demonstrative proof (burhān).
references: Bouyges, M., Averroès: Tahafot at-Tahafot, Beyrouth, 1930
Van den Bergh, S., Averroes' Tahafut al-Tahafut, 1954

manuscripts.title_turkish: Kitâbü't-Teysîr fi'l-Müdâvât ve't-Tedbîr (Tedavi ve Sağlık Rehberi)
manuscripts.author: Ebû Mervân Abdülmelik bin Zühr (Avenzoar)
manuscripts.illustration_description: Contains clinical case notes, diagnostic protocols, and post-mortem observations.
manuscripts.subject: Medicine & Experimental Pathology
manuscripts.latin_translation: Liber Teisir (translated into Hebrew by Jacob Frances, then Latin by John of Capua, Venice 1490)
manuscripts.historical_importance: Pioneered experimental tracheotomy on animals (goats); first clinical description of pericarditis, mediastinal tumors, and the scabies mite (Sarcoptes scabiei).
references: Colin, G., La medecine de l'occident musulman: Ibn Zohr, Paris, 1911

manuscripts.author: Ebû Muhammed Câbir bin Eflah el-İşbîlî (Geber)
manuscripts.illustration_description: Geometric proofs, spherical trigonometry diagrams, and planetary orbit corrections.
manuscripts.subject: Astronomy & Spherical Trigonometry
manuscripts.latin_translation: Gebri Filii Affla Hispalensis de Astronomia Libri IX (Gerard of Cremona, printed Nuremberg 1534)
manuscripts.historical_importance: Invented Geber's theorem for right spherical triangles (cos A = cos a · sin B); placed Venus and Mercury above the Sun instead of below based on lack of observable parallax.
references: Lorch, R. P., Jabir ibn Aflah and the Establishment of Trigonometry in the West, 1975
